name: Seeed reTerminal E1003
description: 10.3 inch monochrome ePaper terminal with 16-level greyscale (IT8951 controller), ESP32-S3, up to six-month battery, 1872x1404 native landscape. Pairs with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF build (unified firmware) and speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API. Server-side pack via esp32_gray_bin produces a raw 4-bpp linear grayscale buffer (1314144 bytes) the firmware streams straight into the IT8951's image buffer.
notes_md: Confirmed on real hardware running tesserae-device-firmware, including touch input (GT911). Wire format is exactly 1314144 bytes (1872*1404/2), row-major, top-left origin, no mirror. Per byte: high nibble = LEFT pixel, low nibble = RIGHT pixel; nibble value 0x0 = black, 0xF = white, linear 16-level grayscale. The firmware handles any physical panel-side mirror; the renderer keeps a normal orientation so a browser preview and the panel paint agree. Historically the E1003 was routed through TRMNL BYOS + trmnl_png (mono 1-bit); the unified firmware supersedes that path for this panel.

touch_enabled.label: Touch input
touch_enabled.help: Wake on touch and dispatch taps/swipes against the dashboard's touch regions. Keeps the touch controller powered through deep sleep (a few mA continuous), which materially reduces battery life; best on USB power.

touch_linger_s.label: Touch linger
touch_linger_s.help: Seconds to stay awake after a touch interaction so follow-up taps skip the deep-sleep wake latency (~2.7 s boot + WiFi on this board). 0 sleeps immediately. Only applies while touch input is enabled.

beep_enabled.label: Beep on interaction
beep_enabled.help: Sound the on-board buzzer the moment a touch or a button press registers, before the server is contacted. E-ink takes seconds to repaint, so without it there is no confirmation the panel heard you. Off by default: a panel that starts beeping unannounced is worse than a silent one.

beep_tone.label: Beep tone
beep_tone.help: Which sound to make. The server sends the actual notes, so these are editable without a firmware update. The buzzer is a passive piezo, loudest around 2 kHz.

beep_pattern.label: Custom tone
beep_pattern.help: Only used when the tone is set to Custom. Notes as frequency:milliseconds pairs, comma separated, e.g. 1800:30,2600:40. A frequency of 0 is a rest. Up to 8 notes, 200-8000 Hz, 1 second total.

beep_volume.label: Beep volume
beep_volume.help: Drive strength as a percentage. The piezo is loudest at 100 and audible but discreet around 30; 0 is silent, same as turning the beep off.
